question: What is the budgetary disinvestment target of the Union government of India for FY20?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1,05,000 crore**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The budgetary disinvestment target of the Union government of India for FY20 is **₹1,05,000 crore**.
 
• This target was set to help the government meet its fiscal deficit goals and to generate revenue by selling stakes in public sector enterprises.
 
• Disinvestment involves the sale of government stakes in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to private entities or the general public.
 
• The funds generated from disinvestment are often used to finance various government expenditures and to reduce the fiscal burden.
 
• The target for FY20 was one of the highest set by the Indian government, reflecting its commitment to fiscal prudence and economic reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Disinvestment targets are announced annually as part of the Union Budget.
 
• The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) is responsible for overseeing disinvestment processes in India.
 
• Disinvestment helps in improving the efficiency and competitiveness of PSUs by involving private sector management practices.
 
• The proceeds from disinvestment can also be used for social and infrastructure development programs.
 
• In recent years, strategic disinvestment has been emphasized, where a substantial portion of government stakes in certain PSUs is sold to strategic partners.
